narrative.overview:
Each Oracle Cloud quarterly release buries hundreds of FBDI field changes across dozens of template files. This report's entire purpose is to extract the signal — exactly what changed, in exactly which field, at exactly which position — and deliver it with the authority of Definian's brand. The design system exists to serve that extraction: nothing decorative, nothing ambient, nothing that slows a consultant's read-through.

The system is built on the Definian canonical palette — Authority Blue, Signal Green, and their four supporting neutrals — supplemented by two semantic additions: Caution Amber for modified fields and Remove Red for removals. Color is the primary semantic layer; shape and spacing are structure. The system is deliberately flat, tightly typeset, and unambiguous about hierarchy.

HTML and PDF are treated as separate media. A consultant running the HTML report in a browser gets interaction and space; a consultant printing the PDF gets density and legibility. The one thing constant across both: an unmistakable Definian visual signature.
keyCharacteristics: Flat tonal depth — no shadows, surfaces differentiated by background color alone
Semantic color system — every color has one job and never doubles as decoration
Mono for machines — all technical identifiers in monospace
Definian brand through structure — blue headers, green accents, the palette does the branding work
Two-medium design — HTML and PDF optimized independently for their respective audiences

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Color carries semantic meaning, never decoration. Green = added/positive, Red = removed/critical, Amber = modified/caution, Blue = structure/authority.

rules.name: The Six Plus Two Rule
rules.body: The six canonical Definian colors are primary. Caution Amber and Remove Red are the only approved supplementals. Any future semantic extension must be documented.

rules.name: The No Off-Palette Rule
rules.body: Introducing a color outside the eight documented tokens is prohibited without explicit justification and documentation.

rules.name: The Mono Rule
rules.body: Every technical identifier — Oracle field name, Applaud column name, table prefix, filename — must render in monospace. A field name in regular sans is a defect.

rules.name: The Label Rule
rules.body: All column headers and structural sub-labels are uppercase with letter-spacing ≥0.5px. Breaking this disrupts the visual contract with the reader.

rules.name: The Flat Signal Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow anywhere. If you need to distinguish a surface, use a background color shift or a 1px Mist Divider border.

dos: Do use Authority Blue (#0D2C71) for all structural headers, file head bars, table column fills, and section h2 headings.
Do use Signal Green (#00AB63) only for ADDED field counts and labels, Financials module identification, and the cover brand wordmark.
Do render every Oracle field name, Applaud column name, table prefix, and filename in monospace.
Do use uppercase + letter-spacing ≥0.5px for all table column headers and structural sub-labels.
Do use 1px solid #D8D7EE for all surface containment borders.
Do use Cloud Surface (#F7F7FB) for all card-like backgrounds.
Do treat HTML and PDF as separate design targets — optimize each for its medium.
Do use Midnight (#02072D) — not #000 — for all body text.
donts: Don't use border-left greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on cards, panels, or callouts. Side-stripe borders are prohibited.
Don't use Signal Green decoratively. Once it appears on a non-addition element, its semantic value is gone.
Don't use box-shadow anywhere. The system is flat.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient). All text is a single solid color.
Don't introduce a ninth color without documenting its semantic role.
Don't render the cover gradient as flat Authority Blue — the gradient is earned.
Don't add decoration that carries no semantic meaning.
Don't add a new change-type label in body weight or mixed case — all change labels are uppercase, weight 700, Label scale.
